extractions.value: Our patient fulfills all the criteria for the diagnosis of stiff person syndrome. The continuous motor unit activity in the EMG was abolished by spinal anaesthesia, but showed no Significant reduction cither by natural sleep or sleep induced by intravenous diazepam, suggesting a central spinal cord origin for the spontaneous activity. The silent periods in the muscles of the lower limbs were absent suggesting loss of interneuronal inhibition.

extractions.value: Concentric needle EMG at rest; intravenous diazepam (40 mg) effect on CMUA; pavlon (0.1 mg/kg) with venous return occluded by blood pressure cuff; spinal anaesthesia (3 ml of 2% xylocaine); silent period of thenar muscles (median nerve supramaximal stimulation, thumb abduction against resistance) and flexor hallucis (posterior tibial nerve supramaximal stimulation).
extractions.quote: Electromyography using concentric needle electrodes... Forty milligrams of intravenous diazepam produced partial reduction of the continuous motor unit activity. The blood pressure cuff was applied to the arm and the pressure was elevated to 10 mm above the systolic blood pressure. The cuff was retained al this pressure for approximately 5 minutes during which time pavlon 0.1 mg/kg body weight was administered intravenously in the flow- occluded limb... Spinal anaesthesia using 3 ml of 2% xylocaine precipitated flaccidity of both lower limbs with electromyographic electrical silence in the muscle sampled... Silent period of the thenar group of muscles elicited by stimulating the median nerve supramaximally with the patient maintaining the thumb in abduction against resistance were of normal duration (128 to 143 m sec). No silent periods could be demonstrated in the flexor hallucis by stimulating the posterior tibial nerve supramaximally.
